newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Vietnam seen to settle border dispute soon.
newsitem.headline: China, Vietnam seen to settle border dispute soon.

text.p: China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen has told visiting Vietnamese Deputy Foreign Minister Vu Khoan that disputes over common land and maritime borders can be settled soon, the People's Daily said on Saturday.
"Qian said he is convinced that...(border) issues remaining from the past can be settled as soon as possible," Xinhua said.
Qian did not give a timetable or say how border disputes would be settled.

Tensions between China and Vietnam, which fought a border war in 1979, have eased in recent years, but territorial issues along the land and sea borders dividing the communist neighbours have continued to hamper rapprochement.
Vu Khoan arrived in Beijing on Tuesday to attend the fifth round of government-level boundary negotiations, which Xinhua said were held in a "friendly and frank atmosphere".
Qian said China and Vietnam faced similar tasks of developing their economies and needed "a long-term stable and peaceful international environment".

"Settling boundary issues between China and Vietnam is in the fundamental interest of the people of the two countries and is the wish of the leaders and the peoples of both countries," Xinhua quoted Qian as saying.
Tension between Beijing and Hanoi boiled over in March, when a Chinese oil rig began exploratory drilling in a South China Sea area Vietnam claims as its own.
The rig was withdrawn after less than a month, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences on the issue at an emergency meeting in Beijing in April.
The potential wealth in oil and natural gas of the offshore areas claimed by China and Vietnam has been a constant threat to recent efforts by both countries to boost ties.
Fishing rights in the waters between the two countries are also a long-time dispute.
